title: Manuel Perez and his reading band
summary: Howard recalls Perez's reading band, the six-eight marches and hymns at funerals, and his dance work.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You see that baby? I was gonna ask about Manuel Perez, did you ever hear him much?
How late did he play? Was he playing much in the 30's? Did you ever see him turn off a little? I wonder, did he play many parades? Did you remember hearing him much on the street or in dances?
Yeah, yeah. Manuel had a musical band.
I never got to hear it, so I don't know what he's talking about.
What? No, a musical band, he never played like we play out the street now. Everything was by music, they played those six eights.

They played the six eights, and they played the fuel marches. Played going to get to that body, they played a hymn, maybe when they get near to the place, you know, where the body was. And then they played the fuel marches, when they leave from there, and six eights. Wasn't no rough.
Coming back there from the graveyard, would they ever play, say like Diddy Ramble and all the rough stuff, or did they jazz up the numbers? Well no, not that I know of.

Every time I would, but no, he could jazz. I thought I wanted to be. Yeah, he could jazz, but when they'd be out there they'd be playing that music. They'd be playing that music, like you do now, and all that kind of, you know.
How late did he play around in the streets, and how late did he work with his dance band?
I mean how long since he died, about 1946 I believe, but when did he stop playing? Do you remember when you heard him, how you were?

No, I heard him, I remember he used to play, long years ago, there was different stores, would have a band to play out in front, and so forth like that, and I'd hear him play with six pieces, something like that. Well then he would be playing, you know, jazz, by head or something like that. But when he'd play on the roof guard and all that place up there, the tempo. Oh yeah. Well everybody was reading.
